In summary, our research is concerned with
the discursive construction of nature and its relationship to conservation and sustainable development.
the relationship between local discourses and conservation policies in the context of the Natura 2000 network, which is the largest coordinated network of protected areas in the world.
the ways in which the narratives about nature, and the nature of narratives, influence the ways in which nature is managed, protected and preserved.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the narrative nature of Nature and the narrative nature(s) of Natura 2000 need to be critically analyzed in order to be able to understand the complex relationships that underlie conservation and management in semi-natural environments.
, if the Natura 2000 sites are to be managed in an effective and sustainable manner, the local narratives of the people who live and work there must become part of the management process.

the use of Critical Discourse Analysis is an interesting way to explore and interpret the narratives that are constructed around nature conservation, as well as to understand how these narratives influence decision-making and the development of local policies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the narratives that people use in their daily life, and which constitute their “natural” world, are a key element for the conservation of nature, and that Critical Discourse Analyses may be used as a tool for understanding the dialectical relationship that exists between local narratives and the strategic behavior of decision-makers in spatial and socio-economic decision making processes.
the narratives of local communities are a crucial part of the conservation of biodiversity, but that they need to be understood as part of a larger narrative, that is, the narrative of nature.
the Natura 2000 network of protected areas is not only a network of places, but also a network of narratives, and that it is the narratives that constitute and define the network.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the narratives that emerge from Critical Discourse Analysis can help in identifying local discourses and the social representations that are most likely to support the implementation of conservation strategies.

the analysis of the narratives that constitute the discursive field of a particular place is an essential step toward a better understanding of the dynamics of local conservation and the potential of local actors in promoting sustainable development.

the narratives that emerge from the discursive practices of the various stakeholders involved in decision-making are a crucial element for the success of conservation and sustainable development initiatives.
